**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate peer leases before trusting their path claims**

When a post-implementation commit changes a path claimed by a peer whose lease has expired—or by a peer entry fabricated in an earlier commit—`historical_peer_path(root, parent, ...)` returns true based only on the path claim, so this filter omits the change from `unexpected`; the code can then be reverted and the peer removed before Completion without detection. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the lookup was moved to the parent snapshot, but that peer snapshot is still never required to have a valid admission, active status, or unexpired lease. Validate the peer's complete contemporaneous registration before using its claims to exempt code.

rows.officialBody:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate completed-peer Evidence repairs before exempting them**

When a post-implementation commit rewrites a completed peer's Evidence and a later commit restores it, this unconditional Program-based classification treats both changes as peer work even though the peer has no active registration and no completed-Evidence repair checks are run. The `unexpected` filter consequently drops those paths and Completion can certify a history containing an unauthorized cross-task Evidence rewrite once the final tree is clean; require the commits to satisfy the completed task's same-task Evidence-repair protocol before exempting them.
